title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: FRANK'S TOAST
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Frank Pelletier, a snowplow mechanic in Barre, Vermont.
Frank can fix a plow in a blizzard.
But when his daughter Katie asked him to give the toast at her wedding, his knees turned to oatmeal.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ASK
segments.quote: Courage is not simply one of the virtues, but the form of every virtue at the testing point.
segments.author: C. S. Lewis
lines: Frank said, Ask Uncle Ron. Ron talks to anybody.
That night, his wife Pat read him a line from C. S. Lewis:
Courage is not simply one of the virtues, but the form of every virtue at the testing point.
This is your testing point, Frank.
He called Katie and said yes. Then he had to sit down.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CLUB
segments.quote: All the great speakers were bad speakers at first.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: He joined a speaking club at the library.
His first try lasted forty seconds. He said um thirty-one times. Somebody counted.
Then Marge, a retired auctioneer of eighty-one, quoted Ralph Waldo Emerson:
All the great speakers were bad speakers at first.
Frank came back the next Tuesday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE JOKES
segments.quote: Always be a first-rate version of yourself, instead of a second-rate version of somebody else.
segments.author: Judy Garland
lines: Next, he found twenty jokes online. Nobody laughed. One man checked his watch.
Marge said, The movie star Judy Garland put it best:
Always be a first-rate version of yourself, instead of a second-rate version of somebody else.
So Frank told one true story about Katie instead. The room laughed, then cried.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: 22 PAGES
segments.author: William Strunk Jr.
lines: Now he couldn't stop. His toast grew to twenty-two pages.
Pat handed him her old writing book by William Strunk, with one rule circled:
Omit needless words.
Frank trimmed it like a rusty bolt, down to one index card.
He practiced on the plows. They loved it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PUNCH BOWL
segments.quote: Let us say what we feel, and feel what we say; let speech harmonize with life.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Wedding day. Frank stood up, hands shaking, and dropped his card. Right into the punch bowl.
Two hundred people waited. He remembered Seneca, the Roman thinker:
Let us say what we feel, and feel what we say; let speech harmonize with life.
So he left the card in the punch, and just talked to his daughter.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FIRST DANCE
segments.quote: Certain it is, that there is no kind of affection so pure and angelic as that of a father to a daughter.
segments.author: Joseph Addison
lines: He told them about the blizzard Katie rode in his plow all night.
She'd said, Dad, you never leave anybody stuck. He toasted her husband Luis: Now she's got someone who won't either.
Pat whispered Joseph Addison, the old English writer:
Certain it is, that there is no kind of affection so pure and angelic as that of a father to a daughter.
So Frank, who swore he'd never dance, asked Katie to dance. Badly. Nobody counted.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Keep going. Be yourself. Cut the extra. Speak from the heart. Dance anyway.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes when it scares you. Keep going. Be yourself. Cut the extra. Speak from the heart. And dance anyway.
I once gave a toast so long, the cake went stale.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
